A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 49-page versions of Differentiable Constraint-Based Causal Discovery. Their main text, appendices, equations, figures, tables, and checklist support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original DAGPA and baseline experiments on synthetic binary data, Sachs, and LUCAS, including numerical tables and empirical CDFs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix C retain the same differentiable d-separation construction, losses, PCGrad optimization, discrete Langevin sampling, and DAG-selection procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ER/SF synthetic binary graph settings, Sachs data, and LUCAS0 benchmark. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain PC, k-PC with k=1 and k=2, GES, and linear/nonlinear NOTEARS and DAGMA. Changed citation numbers do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same graph configurations, sample sizes, preprocessing, CI-testing descriptions, evaluation metrics, and DAG-selection settings.

E4.justification: Appendix F.1 retains the analyses relating CI-MCC and DAG-selection scores to graph-structure metrics. Appendix G.2.1 retains the same normalization-robustness evidence; no supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Repeated-dataset and initialization counts, empirical CDF reporting, and tabulated uncertainty reporting are unchanged. No additional statistical procedure or uncertainty disclosure appears.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the empirical figures retain identical results and curves. Figure 4's corrected panel references do not change its findings or numerical evidence.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, lower-bound and consistency results, Appendix A proofs, Appendix B derivations, and Appendix C.5 complexity analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same differentiable d-separation contribution and claims about robustness in low-sample regimes and performance on Sachs.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including the p-value heuristics, low-order conditioning, absence of confounders, and scalability concerns. The Figure 4 correction preserves the existing interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D retain the same implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information, and code/data access link. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same research positioning, including the identical GOLEM discussion. Revisions to its bibliography entry, Fisher deduplication, and Sener–Koltun publication metadata are bibliographic corrections rather than changes in related-work coverage.

P1.justification: v2 removes the duplicate Fisher reference, revises bibliographic details for the retained GOLEM and Sener–Koltun citations, and updates the version/date stamp. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4's caption corrects reversed panel references: the high-sample setting is panel (b), and the low-sample setting is panel (a). Bibliography edits cause limited reflow; figures, table structures, and graphical content otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects Figure 4's misleading panel references so the caption agrees with the plotted sample sizes and existing results discussion. Bibliographic cleanup also improves presentation. These are limited accuracy improvements; the methods, theoretical support, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
